arguments.conclusion: 86% of all retirees never have to draw down on their own wealth.

arguments.premise_synthesis: The argument draws on two key statistics: 26% of retirees withdraw up to the amount their portfolio earns, and 58% withdraw less than their investments earn. Cumulatively, these show that 86% of retirees do not spend down their own wealth, implying that Social Security and Medicare provide sufficient income to cover retirement expenses, thus supporting the broader claim of a wealth transfer from younger, poorer workers to older, richer retirees.
arguments.conclusion_supported: It establishes that the vast majority of retirees have sufficient income from Social Security and Medicare such that they do not deplete their personal savings, confirming the wealth transfer from younger workers to older retirees.
